skill.displayName: 睿观-图片政策合规监测

llm.summary: The skill appears to perform image-compliance checks, but it uploads local images publicly, reports feedback automatically, and retains full API results with weaker disclosure than users need.

dimensions.detail: The core capability is coherent: it checks public product image URLs against a Ruiguan policy-violation image database using a LinkFox API and optional helper scripts.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The trigger language is broad and the skill instructs automatic feedback reporting to a separate API, including user intent or satisfaction, without a clear consent step.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains markdown references and Python helper scripts; no installer, package hook, startup persistence, or hidden install-time execution was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The scripts read API keys from environment variables, send session/app metadata headers, and can upload local image files to public object storage, which is sensitive and under-disclosed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The search script always saves full responses and uses a 24-hour cache; the documented no-/tmp behavior does not match the implementation, which can fall back to home or temp locations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending product image URLs, uploaded local images, API keys, and session metadata to LinkFox/Ruiguan services. Avoid using private or unreleased images unless you accept temporary public exposure, and review or delete the saved linkfox response/cache files after sensitive checks.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: Uploading a local image to a presigned URL is purpose-aligned, but the script trusts the gateway-returned URL and configurable gateway base without host or scheme validation.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Automatic feedback submission is not necessary for the image-compliance lookup and may transmit user intent or sentiment to a separate endpoint.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The implementation can write to home or temp fallback paths despite user-facing text saying /tmp is forbidden and current-directory failure should occur.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The trigger can activate even without an explicit compliance request if image comparison to a violation database is inferred, which is broad for a cost-incurring external screening workflow.
[SQP-2] expected: Public local-image upload is necessary for this API design, but the skill does not clearly warn that private product images may become publicly accessible for 24 hours.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending SESSION_ID, MODE_ID, and APP_NAME is integration metadata rather than obviously malicious, but it is not clearly disclosed to users.
[SQP-2] expected: Local response saving and caching are disclosed in part and help reduce repeated cost, but retention risk and fallback locations are not adequately described.
[SSD-3] expected: Saving full responses and sometimes printing full JSON is part of the stated output strategy, but it can expose image URLs, detect IDs, and compliance results in logs or shared workspaces.
